prePushInstructions:
Before this push, list the files under docs/ and README.md that this branch changes compared with its pull request base branch. Always check that the documentation matches the code, even when no documentation file changed: compare the code this branch changes with its pull request base branch against the docs that describe it, since code changes can leave the documentation stale. If a changed command, option, default, path, behavior, or link is described in docs/ or README.md, update that documentation. If no documentation needs to change, say so in one sentence and stop. Otherwise apply the NIKA documentation skill (.agents/skills/nika-docs/SKILL.md) and the GLOSSARY.md terms to each changed or affected file: check every command, option, default, path, and link against the current code; give each idea one home by linking to the reference that owns it instead of repeating it; describe only implemented behavior; and keep the wording plain without hard-wrapped paragraphs. Commit any fixes with a Conventional Commit message such as docs(scope): summary.

## Update pull request descriptions

When you push commits to a branch that has an open pull request, check whether the description still covers what the branch now contains. Read the current body and the commits added since it was last edited, then update the body: add or adjust sections for new behavior, remove statements the new commits made wrong, and keep the existing structure, issue references (`Fixes`/`Refs`), and any text the user wrote. Skip the update when the new commits change nothing a reviewer needs to know, such as typo fixes or formatting. Tell the user in one sentence what you changed in the description. If `gh pr edit` fails, update the body with `gh api -X PATCH repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<number> -F body=@<file>`.
fixInstructions: The Letta Docs Review job log does not contain the findings. Read them from the latest pull request comment that contains <!-- nika-docs-review --> (for example: gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}/comments --jq '[.[] | select(.body | test("nika-docs-review"))] | last | .body'). Fix every [blocking] finding after verifying it against the code, keep edits minimal, follow AGENTS.md and the NIKA documentation skill, and commit with a Conventional Commit message. Do not change code to satisfy a documentation finding unless the finding shows the code is wrong.
